title: Why easy studying creates weak memory
hook: Feeling fluent after rereading? That ease often lies.
cta: Save this and try one change today

slides.title: Why 'Easy' Study Fails Memory
slides.body: Fluency after rereading or cramming masks weak, short‑lived memory. Effortful retrieval makes learning stick.

slides.title: Fluency is a familiarity trick
slides.body: Rereading boosts processing ease but not recall strength. Familiarity feels like knowing but fails when you must produce answers.

slides.title: Retrieval beats re-exposure
slides.body: Actively trying to recall information strengthens memory traces far more than passive re‑exposure does.

slides.title: Cramming gives short gains
slides.body: Massed practice inflates session performance but causes rapid forgetting. Spacing forces retrieval across time and improves retention.

slides.title: Context limits future cues
slides.body: Studying in only one format ties memory to that context. Use different prompts and formats to broaden retrieval cues.

slides.title: Aim for desirable difficulty
slides.body: Make practice slightly challenging but attainable: closed‑book recall, short summaries, or brief self‑quizzes before checking answers.

slides.title: Memorable Takeaway
slides.body: Easy studying feels productive but builds fragile memory. Prioritize spaced, effortful retrieval with corrective feedback. What's one study habit you'll change?
slides.footer: Save this for your next study session

caption:
Quick practical checklist:
• Replace one reread with a closed‑book recall.
• Space that recall across days.
• Add a brief self‑test before checking answers.
